transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jorge (VanguardAI CTO), Sara (Head of Compliance), Anil (DevOps), Mina (PM)

Summary (auto): weekly pilot check-in, focus on security/compliance and perf tuning.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jorge: Doing good thanks, little hectic but ready.
[00:12] Maya: Cool. The agenda today, quick status on SSO, audit logs export view, retention policy, and then Liam will walk through the perf test plan and we can schedule the on-prem connectivity test. Anything else to add?
[00:25] Sara: I wanna flag SOC two evidence, we need to see the recent reports and how you surface events for our auditors.
[00:32] Liam: Yep, we'll pull screenshots of the audit log UI and also provide an obfuscated CSV dump.
[00:38] Anil: Also need to confirm IP ranges for our firewall, and whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS or HSM.
[00:45] Maya: Great, all on the list. Quick SSO update — Priya, wanna give the status?
[00:52] Priya: Sure. We got the SAML metadata from Jorge yesterday, we imported it into our dev tenant and did a test login, there was a small cert mismatch that we fixed. Right now the dev SSO is green but staging still has an attribute mapping issue — email vs userPrincipalName mapping. Should be resolved by EOD tomorrow once Jorge confirms the mapping he wants.
[01:15] Jorge: Yeah we want email to be the primary ID. I think our IdP sends mail instead of email, sometimes abbreviations, so we'll normalize.
[01:23] Priya: Right, that's the little mismatch. Also note the session duration defaults to one hour in the dev token — we can tune that or make it configurable per customer.
[01:32] Sara: On the audit logs, can you confirm retention windows? Our compliance policy needs at least 7 years for certain transaction logs, and a shorter window for non-critical metadata.
[01:44] Maya: Good question. Currently in the hosted pilot the default is 90 days for full text transcripts and 2 years for metadata, but for enterprise pilots we can configure longer retention or export hooks to your S3.
[01:58] Sara: Export hooks to our S3 would be ideal, we prefer to own the long-tail retention. But we need proof that logs are immutable and tamper-evident.
[02:09] Liam: On immutability — we push logs with write-once flags to the storage we control in private deployments, and for hosted we generate signed manifests and SHA checksums for each archive. The UI shows an audit chain but I know auditors like paper trails; we'll include exportable manifests.
[02:30] Jorge: Is the manifest stored separately from the archive? We need separation to prove non-repudiation.
[02:35] Liam: Yes, manifest is computed client-side and the hash is stored in Redwood's audit index plus you can have a copy pushed to customer S3. So you get two anchors.
[02:45] Anil: About KMS — do you integrate with AWS KMS or can we bring our own HSM? Latency is a concern if keys are remote.
[02:53] Maya: We support customer-managed KMS via provider integrations for AWS, GCP, and Azure. For HSM, it's supported on Private deployments; it's a feature flag and requires some network configuration.
[03:05] Mina: For the pilot we may want to test both — hosted with envelope encryption to our KMS, and an on-prem instance later.
[03:12] Priya: That makes sense. For envelope encryption, the egress latency for token generation is negligible, but when we do RSA unwraps on each ephemeral session it can add a few milliseconds. We'll run numbers for the pilot.
[03:26] Sara: Also need RBAC mapping to our groups — we don't want every engineer to see full transcripts.
[03:32] Maya: RBAC is supported, we have roles at token, team, and org levels. You can restrict transcript visibility to only audit and compliance roles. There is a caveat with older logs pre-archival.
[03:44] Jorge: Great. On the perf side, Liam, can you walk through the KV cache / batching test plan?
[03:50] Liam: Sure. For the pilot we ran a baseline with KV cache off, 4k context, 8 concurrent streams. Results were steady but latency varied. We're proposing to enable KV cache and continuous batching for the next run, target is sub-200ms median token latency for short prompts and no tail spikes over 800ms. We'll do 1-hour sustained run with synthetic traffic and then a mixed workload run using your sample prompt set.
[04:18] Jorge: Sounds good. Any impacts on cost modeling?
[04:21] Liam: Enabling KV cache reduces token compute and cost by ~22% in our estimate; batching can improve throughput but may increase median latency slightly if requests are micro-bursty. We'll provide a cost/latency matrix.
[04:35] Mina: For the mixed workload, can we include edge cases where prompts are 12k tokens? We want to see behavior for longer contexts.
[04:42] Liam: We can simulate long contexts but some models will degrade; we'll test with a 12k checkpoint and also a 8k quantized variant.
[04:50] Sara: Back to audit logs — what fields are included in the event stream? We need user id, request_id, model, tokens consumed, and redact flags.
[04:59] Priya: The event schema includes timestamp, user_id, request_id, model_id, config hash, token_count, prompt_hash, and an obfuscated prompt reference. We avoid full prompt storage unless you opt-in. For PII we have masking rules and a redact flag.
[05:18] Sara: Ok, but auditors will want sample rows. Can you provide a CSV with PII masked?
[05:23] Maya: Yes, that's one of the action items — we'll share an obfuscated export.
[05:27] Anil: On the network side, what IP ranges should I open? Also, will the on-prem connector use outbound-only connections?
[05:36] Liam: For hosted dev it's a set of CIDR blocks we'll share; for private it's an outbound-only TLS tunnel to a regional endpoint, so you only need to allow outbound to a small set of endpoints on 443. We'll provide the exact list.
[05:50] Jorge: What's the plan for SOC two evidence? Sara, any specific artifacts beyond reports?
[05:56] Sara: We want configuration snapshots, access logs, change logs, and evidence of backup retention policies. Also proof of encryption at rest and in transit, and key rotation policies.
[06:10] Maya: Redwood can provide SOC 2 type II report redacted for customer-specific data, and we can produce config snapshots for the pilot environment. We'll need a data processing addendum signed for some proof artifacts though.
[06:23] Sara: Fine, we'll route that to legal.
[06:27] [07:00] -- [note: conversation moves into scheduling and clarifications] --
[07:03] Mina: Quick note on data residency — part of our customers need EU-only processing. For this pilot, is the hosted option in EMEA available?
[07:13] Maya: Yes, we have EMEA region; for the pilot we can pin to that region. Private on-prem would also meet residency.
[07:20] Anil: If we do on-prem later, will logs still be forwarded to our SIEM? We want integration with Splunk.
[07:27] Priya: We have Splunk forwarder integrations and generic syslog/S3 sink. We'll give you sample config.
[07:34] Jorge: Good. Any concerns about vendor lock-in? Some folks worry about model artifacts and provider-specific quantization.
[07:42] Liam: We try to be model-agnostic: we support model export in standard weights and a compatibility layer; quantization is optional and documented. For portability, we can provide model artifacts and conversion steps at the end of pilot.
[07:55] Sara: That helps. Can you confirm retention partitioning so that PII transcripts are purged earlier if required?
[08:02] Priya: Yes, we can configure retention policies per data class: PII, low-sensitivity, audit-only. For hosted pilot we can set up rules and push full transcripts to your S3 with lifecycle rules.
[08:15] Jorge: Ok let's talk timeline. We want the KV cache perf test this week, SSO mapping resolved by tomorrow, and the audit export by Friday.
[08:24] Maya: That's doable. Liam will run the perf test, I'll export logs and SOC2 artifacts, and Anil will send network ranges.
[08:33] Anil: I'll send IP list and KMS endpoint details by Tuesday.
[08:38] Sara: I'll confirm retention windows internally and get back to you.
[08:42] Maya: Great. Any blockers?
[08:45] Jorge: Not from product side. Just want to ensure encryption and RBAC are ironed out before we expand test volume.
[08:54] Priya: Yep understood. We'll attach a sample RBAC mapping doc to the ticket.
[08:59] Liam: For the perf run, heads up: we'll enable KV cache and run two phases — synthetic then feed your prompt set. Expect a short outage while we toggle cache warm-up, maybe 30s to a minute of higher latency.
[09:14] Mina: Fine as long as it's scheduled.
[09:17] Maya: Alright, recap of next steps: Redwood share audit log export + screenshots, run KV cache perf test and share results, provide SSO attribute mapping guide and confirm staging fix, share IP ranges and KMS details, and schedule the on-prem connectivity test.
[09:33] Jorge: Good. Anything else?
[09:36] Sara: One more: can we get a brief write-up on your manifest format and how auditors should verify the checksums?
[09:44] Liam: We'll add a short README and verification script.
[09:49] Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and update the pilot tracker.
[09:54] Jorge: Thanks all.
[09:56] (call ends)

-- End transcript --
notes: Customer specifically asked for immutable audit manifests and an obfuscated CSV sample; discussed KMS/HSM support on Private deployments; Redwood agreed to run KV cache perf test and provide SOC2 artifacts. Some transcription glitches in names (idp vs IdP reported as 'eye-dee-pee') noted.
